questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important factor was to find an  organisation/research center that I found interesting which did not have to be in a specific place but it was rather important for me to be in a country where there are interesting organisations and things going on and Brussels was definitely one of those. Also, being able to either speak the language or refresh a language I know a bit (which was the case with french in Brussels).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some tasks were not very study-related/academic as it happens very often in internships.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine as the unviversity had some good communication regarding exchange students. But as I was an intern and not really a student I did not consider the information that relevant. Most information I got from my boss at the research center.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only from my supervisor at the institution but she was also quite busy. And then again, some general information from the international office of the University of Brussels.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think the orientation you got was good (emails about opening hours for specific questions etc) but I did not really make use of it as I was an intern.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult, but I searched through facebook groups, put up my own add and therefore got contacted by a flatshare.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you are doing an internship, I think it is actually good to be living off campus as you are not really living the student life as such but working

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not receive any orientation regarding the housing and also, it seemed quite expensive and competitive so in this sense I could not really tell how satisfying the options were as I had hardly any information about them. I only got contacted by the university when I had already arrived so at that point I had already found housing (I had to already check and find something in the summer). If people start looking in advance it could be a different situation and housing on campus could be relevant

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In total I found it quite a bit fo work as you had some bureaucratic effort on top of the Erasmus application itself etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to fill in a contract and that was pretty much it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration office and my supervisor at the host institution.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not register for any classes as I was doing an internship.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In general to look for an internship earlier in order to plan all the bureaucratic steps, housing etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really take any courses but looked into some which seemed good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There was no level as I did not do any.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The one course I visited seemed more like a bigger course with a different exam style, more focus on international students (in general at the university) and bigger master programs than in the case of ours here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: General costs were higher in Brussels.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was higher than expected as well as public transport.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The campus was well equipped with a sports hall, a language center and a choir practicing there (to name a few of many opportunities)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sports, welcome activities, choir, languages

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: sports, choir, book club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around belgium by train (everything is so easily accessible)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy due to a nice community that welcomed me at the research center (my work)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the welcoming events, follow welcoming events on website, join some kind of club

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of french

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The dual language aspect

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Use the university opportunities, keep track of what is going on from the beginning

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: How the university functions, how courses can be visited, events going on at the university

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting an insight into a new unviersity, research environment, country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Bureacracy at the beginning, getting used to a new campus and new university system

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
